capture.final_message:
Use two standard representations, proving each component independently.

For the analytic conjunct, apply Abel summation to
\[
\theta(x)=\sum_{p\le x}\log p.
\]
Since \(\pi(t)=\operatorname{primeCounting}(\lfloor t\rfloor)\) for real \(t\ge2\), summation by parts gives
\[
\theta(x)=\pi(x)\log x-\int_2^x\frac{\pi(t)}t\,dt.
\]
The floor-function discontinuities are harmless for the interval integral; alternatively, partition at the finitely many integers up to \(\lfloor x\rfloor\).

For the polynomial conjunct, work first with the universal integer polynomial \(U_n\). The Chebyshev differential equation
\[
(1-X^2)U_n''-3XU_n'+n(n+2)U_n=0
\]
implies, after differentiating \(k\) times and evaluating at \(X=0\),
\[
U_n^{(k+2)}(0)
=\big((k+1)^2-(n+1)^2\big)U_n^{(k)}(0),
\]
which is exactly the first side of the stated iff. The integer-index extension, most transparently obtained from the Laurent representation of \(U_n\) or its recurrence, gives
\[
U_{-m-2}=-U_m;
\]
putting \(m=n-1\) yields the second side. Prove these identities over \(\mathbb Z[X]\) and transport them to every commutative ring, avoiding any characteristic or division assumptions.

Finally, the two propositions inside the iff are both unconditional universal identities, so each implication may simply invoke the independently established identity; no direct logical conversion between them is needed.
